# Compile a weekly summary: Discord

**Pattern:** Scheduled Digest · **Level:** Intermediate · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers digests work end to end across Discord, Google Sheets and Google Drive.

It moves through 15 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Gather from Google Drive
3. Roll Up KPIs
4. Compose HTML Report
5. Send Report via Discord
6. Guard Non-Empty severity
7. Sort Events Newest First
8. Tag Pipeline Metadata
9. Align Field Names
10. Cap Batch Volume
11. Stamp Processing Time
12. Save Execution Metadata
13. Summarize Run Stats
14. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
15. Send Summary to Discord

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Discord — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing digests work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Gather from Google Drive → Roll Up KPIs → Compose HTML Report → Send Report via Discord → Guard Non-Empty severity → Sort Events Newest First → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Align Field Names → Cap Batch Volume → Stamp Processing Time → Save Execution Metadata → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Discord → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Discord

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Discord and Google Sheets aligned by hand for digests
- Digests work where "Gather from Google Drive" is still a manual step before Discord
- Digests work that only reaches Discord on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Discord and Google Sheets in step for digests, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Discord or Google Sheets call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 17 nodes in this digests build
- Every digests run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Discord
- Fans the same result out to Google Drive in the same run, for digests
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 17 nodes for digests before wiring Discord

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Discord webhook URL; Google OAuth2; Google OAuth2 / service account.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

KPIs are rolled up with Summarize (exact group-by + aggregate) before any AI touches the data — asking an LLM to 'figure out the numbers' from raw records is slower, costlier, and less reliable than doing exact arithmetic in n8n and only asking the model to narrate numbers that are already correct.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Add a second data source and watch it blend into the same report via Merge.
2. Toggle the AI executive-summary step on and off and compare the report's usefulness.
3. Change the KPI grouping field and see how the pivot reshapes.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Drive API → OAuth2 client or Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Service Accounts have their own empty Drive — share the target folder with it.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy URL.
_Gotcha:_ Webhook mode needs no bot token. Messages cap at 2000 characters.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your digests process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Discord: give the bot access to the destination channel only, not the whole guild.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Google Drive: scope the credential to the one folder this workflow writes to, not `drive.readonly` across the account.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole digests payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
